models_evaluated: nine widely used LLMs (names not given in the abstract)

links.outcome: Readability and actionability of LLM-generated cardiac myxoma patient education texts
links.effect: Texts showed significant heterogeneity in quality, understandability and objective readability; clinical actionability was generally low. Reading-difficulty indices were negatively correlated with PEMAT-P actionability. Ideally suited texts were a very small proportion of outputs.
links.quote: Within this expert-curated educational question set, the current application of LLMs in patient education for cardiac myxoma is primarily limited by reading burden and insufficient behavioral guidance.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of nine LLMs generating patient education texts on cardiac myxoma, measuring text quality, readability, and actionability against standardized assessment tools without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
